roles.producer: Builds AI models where the model is the product or a core asset, or where the model is distributed to others (API, open weights, embedded in products).
roles.consumer: Uses AI. Not a lower tier of producer: a different question set. Fine-tuning an existing model for own use (internal domain model, PoC) is consumer with the self_hosted modifier; a company whose product is a tuned model that others receive is a producer.

capability.base: LLM use with no access beyond the prompt.
capability.rag: The LLM reads org data through retrieval (RAG, knowledge graph).
capability.mcp: The LLM has tools through MCP or similar: it can read, write and take actions.
capability.agentic: Operates with minimal human oversight; autonomous multi-step work.
capability.note: Each rung includes the ones below. A question's capability is the lowest rung at which it applies. Classic ML and vision models are out of scope.

scope_tags.internal: Day-to-day business processes; output stays inside the org.
scope_tags.code_generation: AI builds or maintains business applications; the output is a persistent executable artifact (insecure code, hallucinated dependencies, licensing, secrets, review gates).
scope_tags.customer_facing: AI inside an app, or output reaching customers or end users, including calling a SaaS LLM API from the org's own app.
scope_tags.third_party_embedded: AI bundled in a tool the org uses (ITSM, ticketing, RPA with a built-in LLM); less control, supply-chain focus.
scope_tags.note: An empty list means the question applies to all usage contexts.

modifiers.builds_on_base_model: Producer builds on an existing base model and inherits upstream risk (licence, inherited bias or safety gaps, base-model change or withdrawal).
modifiers.self_hosted: The org hosts the model or its infrastructure itself, so responsibility shifts from the provider to the org.
modifiers.poc: A proof of concept or experiment, often with real data, a larger exposure surface and fewer checks.
modifiers.unsanctioned_use: Shadow AI: use of AI tools nobody approved.

topics.governance: Oversight, accountability, inventory, impact, third parties and release decisions.
topics.data_model: Data and model protection: RAG and knowledge-graph content, weights, fine-tuned models and prompts are assets.
topics.infra: Protecting where sensitive things are hosted; wording differs for SaaS vs self-hosted.
topics.reliability: Tuning, harness, guardrails, testing; wrong or hostile inputs and outputs, from normal model behaviour or from attack.
topics.ai_access: AI as a new identity with permissions (agents, MCP, RAG): what data it can reach, what it can do, whose permissions it uses, whether a human approves actions.

items.outcome: Information about the AI system’s knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making informed decisions and taking subsequent actions.
suggested_actions: Document settings, environments and conditions that are outside the AI system’s intended use.
Design for end user workflows and toolsets, concept of operations, and explainability and interpretability criteria in conjunction with end user(s) and associated qualitative feedback.
Plan and test human-AI configurations under close to real-world conditions and document results.

Follow stakeholder feedback processes to determine whether a system achieved its documented purpose within a given use context, and whether end users can correctly comprehend system outputs or results.
Document dependencies on upstream data and other AI systems, including if the specified system is an upstream dependency for another AI system or other data.

Document connections the AI system or data will have to external networks (including the internet), financial markets, and critical infrastructure that have potential for negative externalities. Identify and document negative impacts as part of considering the broader risk thresholds and subsequent go/no-go deployment as well as post- deployment decommissioning decisions.

categories.covers: Intended purpose and context of each AI use, who is affected, benefits and harms, impact assessment, fairness and bias in the way outputs are used, human oversight and review of outputs, transparency to users.

AI as a new identity with permissions: what data it can reach, what it can do (read, write, execute), whose permissions it uses (own scoped identity vs the user's full rights), whether a human approves actions, tool and server vetting, audit of actions.

cis_safeguards.title: Establish and Maintain Architecture Diagram(s)
cis_safeguards.ai_applicability: Maintain up-to-date diagrams of LLM system network architecture, including data flows between models, data stores, and external APIs. Accurate diagrams are essential for understanding the attack surface, planning defenses, and conducting incident response in complex AI environments.

cis_safeguards.title: Document Data Flows
cis_safeguards.ai_applicability: Track network segments and storage systems used to host or serve models, including specialized hardware, inference clusters, dedicated GPU nodes, and model artifact storage. Model data and runtime state may reside across distributed storage systems and network zones. Mapping these ensures proper segmentation, backup, access control, and monitoring.

cis_safeguards.title: Document Data Flows
cis_safeguards.ai_applicability: Document end-to-end data flows from tool invocations and resource retrievals through back-end systems into model context. Map servers to their data sources and identify tools that can access sensitive data, noting where content enters prompts. Flag high-risk sources and record resource annotations, including MCP metadata such as audience and priority that indicate intended consumers and handling precedence. cis_safeguards.title: Document Data Flows
cis_safeguards.ai_applicability: Document all retrieval sources, vector stores, indexing pipelines, document loaders, and embedding services used by agents. Track where retrieval content originates and which agents may access it.

cis_safeguards.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Network Architecture
cis_safeguards.ai_applicability: Segment agent runtimes and enforce private, authenticated connectivity for memory and model services. Agents act as the central orchestrator, integrating highly sensitive components like vector databases (memory) and LLM inference endpoints. A secure network architecture must place the agent runtime in a dedicated trust zone, enforcing strict ingress filtering, via ACLs/firewalls, to prevent unauthorized entities from invoking the agent. cis_safeguards.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Network Architecture
cis_safeguards.ai_applicability: Place servers and gateways in dedicated segments protected by firewall rules. Isolate third-party servers from enterprise-developed servers. Where Origin validation is applicable (e.g., browser-mediated clients), enforce strict Origin allowlists; for non-browser clients, enforce client identity using gateway controls, mTLS, or signed workload identity. Restrict local-only servers to `127.0.0.1`. Record network paths for OAuth authorization flows.
